detail.longDescription: Pyright warns me when the annotated return type of a function is narrower than the actual return type. However, it doesn't warn me when it's broader . See this example: class User: def __init__(self, id: int) -> None: self.id = id users: list[User] = [] def get_user(id: int) -> User | None: # forgot to remove `None` user = next((u for u in users if u.id == id), None) if user is None: raise ValueError(f"user {id} not found") return user I had changed the body of get_user to always return a User , but forgot to change the annotation. However, Pyright doesn't tell me that User | None is broader than - and can be simplified to - User . This is expected, because User is assignable to User | None . According to the type annotations docs (emphasis mine): Expressions whose type is assignable to a specific argument type are also accepted for that argument. Similarly, an expression whose type is assignable to the annotated return type can be returned from the function. Can I configure Pyright to detect certain unnecessarily broad annotations, e.g. TypeA | TypeB when just one of the union types is returned?
